title: Spot and preemptible instances: the discount and its price

videos.script: Google sells its spare machines cheaply, on one condition. It can take them back. This lesson is about the discount and the condition. {{discount}} The discount on the sheet is forty to fifty per cent. Spot prices move, so the sum is worth redoing. {{notice}} When Google wants a machine back, it gives thirty seconds of notice. You will watch a program use those seconds well, and another program waste them. {{action}} A preempted machine is stopped or deleted, and you choose which. A time limit of your own stops a stuck job from costing money all night. {{group}} In a group, a lost machine comes back on its own, when there is room. {{fit}} And last, the test. If a machine vanished now, would anyone need to do anything? If not, it belongs on Spot.
